Use 0° for straight sides or 0.5–15° for taper. The face outline, ledge and insertion area stay straight. Only the body behind them tapers. Wall thickness is preserved along the sloping sides. The app reduces the angle when a detail or gap would close. Print back-down and inspect overhangs in your slicer; this feature still needs a physical test.

Checks inside corners and openings against your cutter. Orange areas show material the bit may leave behind. Outlines stay nominal; apply tool compensation in CAM.
A separate flat face that seats on the ledge. Export as STL/3MF; test fit and light diffusion.
Face height relative to rim · mm

Negative: recessed inside. Zero: flush. Positive: raised above the rim. Printed faces have a hollow skirt: twice the face thickness, plus any raised height and extra depth. Raising the face extends the skirt to keep its insertion depth. Cut acrylic remains a flat insert.
Print the face flat on the bed with the skirt growing upwards. Fit clearance is under Fit & attachment. This is a locating skirt, not a click lock.
A collar inside the body. The face stays the same outer size as the body.

Print face-down, flange upwards. Larger allowance means a looser fit. This flange locates the face; it has no click lock. Test the fit sample before printing the whole design. For a flat face without a flange, choose Separate face.
Patterns are currently available for printed faces. CNC and laser faces stay solid.
Hole size is the circle diameter or hexagon corner-to-corner size. A solid border protects outer edges, letter openings and fitting collars. In lightboxes, only the illuminated artwork is perforated.
These are open holes in the printed face and exported files. LEDs can be visible through them. Print a small sample to check strength and lighting. Maximum 2,000 holes per design.

Finish and colour are approximate. This preview does not simulate light diffusion or exact filament colours. Selections are saved in materials.csv and settings.json. STL/3MF exports contain geometry only; assign colours and filament profiles in your slicer.
0.60 mm colour + 2.40 mm backing = 3.00 mm total.

Colour and backing share the total face thickness. Changing either adjusts the other. Change the face thickness in Build; lightboxes include the background thickness. Backing uses the face material colour. Full-depth colour removes the flat backing; push-in fitting collars match the body colour. Test colour-to-colour adhesion and inspect disconnected details. More coloured layers can mean more filament changes.
The coloured side prints on the bed. Start with compatible filaments of the same material. The screen cannot predict transmitted colour or opacity.
Use the multi-plate 3MF or the registered colour STLs in the ZIP. Supports separate faces, outer sleeves, push-in fronts and lightboxes. Splitting and integrated-face bodies are not supported yet.
Adjust these for your printer and actual materials. Dimensions are in millimetres; fit allowances are per side.
The gap is applied around every face edge. Recess moves the face and ledge down without changing body depth.
A loose cap slides over the body. Secure it after fitting.
Zero is nominal contact, negative is tighter, positive is looser. Calibrate before production; this is friction retention, not a snap latch.
The acrylic seats on the body ledge. The cap lip overlaps its front edge; the skirt slips over the body. Total depth includes the front lip. Inner openings may have separate cap rings.
Bond the acrylic to the cap with compatible adhesive. Secure the slip-fit cap with adhesive or shop-drilled retaining screws after testing fit.

The collar presses into the rear opening; the cover stops at the rim. No bosses or holes. Start with a fit test: zero is nominal contact, negative is tighter, positive is looser. Retention depends on the print and material.

Flat cover rests on the rear rim. Screws enter from the back into unthreaded, blind pilot holes. Use pan-head screws; no countersinks or threaded inserts are generated. Match the pilot to your actual screw and test in your filament.
Short bosses sit near the rear with angled supports into the wall. A clear gap remains behind the face. Check actual lighting and screw fit on one letter.

The body expands around the original lettering. Below the front seat, a wider cavity leaves room for strip and wiring. Counter openings are preserved where space permits. Separate or connected inserts may need adhesive or other retention after a fit test.

This mounting needs an accessible fixed-back body. Choose Separate face, Push-in face, Inset face or Acrylic + cap. Rear openings and the full-depth outer sleeve are not supported.
Without screws · slide-in click key · test first
PLA-R3 · 20 mm base. Print the foot, socket and separate locking key samples first. The horizontal key keeps 3.5–3 mm arms and 1.2 mm catches.
Short feet print with the body and seat in the base. Concealed M3 screws secure them from underneath. Wires pass through the feet into the hollow base.
Positive values move the base right or towards the face. Feet stay attached to the sign. The base must contain every socket. A narrower base is not automatically stable; test the assembled sign.
0 = nominal contact. Negative = tighter; positive = looser. Applies to feet and bottom-cover collar. Print both fit samples first.
Each foot needs an M3 × 16 mm screw, flat washer and standard M3 hex nut. Four 2.9 × 8 mm plastic-thread screws hold the bottom cover. Print the mounting sample first.

COB is shown as a continuous light ribbon. Enter your tape width, marked cut interval, voltage and W/m. Standard COB uses straight runs with jumpers; sideways curves need a tape specifically designed for them. Side-wall mounting is not included.
Strip on the inside back, LEDs facing the diffuser. Preview the strip and its bending space before installation.
Simple lightbox · rows or main runs
Open cavities use a few straight rows. Row count overrides target spacing; both at zero use the lighting preference and available depth. Approximate coverage—adjust after a lit test.

Higher values ignore more small branches in the routing guide. The artwork and box stay unchanged. This controls geometry, not lighting coverage. Manual routes take priority; use Automatic in the large editor to regenerate them.
12.50 mm between LED centres · 37.50 mm between cut marks.
Leave consumption blank if unknown. Use W/m from your strip label; changing density does not change consumption automatically.
Starting settings only. Match width, voltage and cutting interval to your actual strip; COB and zig-zag models are not interchangeable.
Use your strip’s marked cut interval. The 8 mm bend radius is a starting value to test, not a verified strip specification.
Letters follow their strokes; simple lightboxes follow the shared cavity. Tight bends stay visible for adjustment instead of being split into small pieces automatically.

Diagnostic overlay stays in assembled position in exploded view. Blue passages already exist in desk-base parts. Purple rear holes are cut into printed parts after Apply & check. Red holes block downloads. Saved holes remain if the LED strip plan is switched off.

Open boxes use straight rows; narrow shapes follow main strokes. Cut lengths round up to the next whole cut group. Extra strip is included in cut length and consumption only; it is not drawn. Red marks a problem with the displayed route. Check flagged bends and junctions; broad areas may need more rows. Lighting uniformity is not simulated.

Dark face colours start as light blocking; other face colours start as light transmitting. Adjust these assumptions for your material. Separate masks, backing and fitting collars do not emit light. Shell sides glow only when Side glow is increased. Multicolour background regions start as light blocking. All regions with the same colour share this choice. Filament, thickness, infill and diffusion affect the real result. Soft glow can be turned off for a lighter preview.

The pocket is cut into the initial. The name must keep enough contact with it, with at least 2 mm of material behind the pocket. Print a small fit test before the full design.

The name inserts into a matching pocket. Zero outside height gives a flush front. At least 2 mm of body remains behind the pocket. Each name piece needs contact with the initial. Chiseled uses a real rock height map for the front. These finishes shape the front, edges and sides. The back stays flat for printing. Finish buttons apply starting settings; adjust them below. Colour is a single filament colour. Granite speckles need effect filament or painting.

Carved grain and tool marks shape the front and sides; the back stays flat. No loose splinters. Finish buttons apply starting settings. Grain angle 0 is vertical; 90 is horizontal. Colour represents one filament, not separately printed grain colours.

These values check detail; choose the matching profile in your slicer. For ordinary PLA, start around 0.12–0.16 mm layers with a 0.4 mm nozzle. Wood-filled filament may require a larger nozzle; follow its manufacturer’s profile. Keep enough top-shell thickness above the infill. Print the flat back on the bed, texture up.
Pattern size controls the overall scale, not the width of every groove. Fine ridges and low relief may disappear in slicing. Preview is ideal geometry; visible layer lines remain on the print.
Same surface settings on a small sample. Textures use a 3 mm base; carved stone and wood use the current body depth to include the sides. Print this first to check finish.
A separate base for one connected main letter. The letter fits into an open slot; no screws. Test fit and balance. The base prints bottom-down.
These colours identify the parts. Choose matching filaments in your slicer. A stone or wood appearance comes from printed geometry; speckles and grain colour require effect filament or finishing.
Plate export tests flat rotations at full size, with an 8 mm edge margin. Oversized parts are blocked; this editor does not split them.
Print back-down. “Solid” means a closed model; set your own infill in the slicer. Check thin features and print a small sample.
Tray and moss styles have a solid floor and open front. Use them for dry decoration; no drainage or food-contact claim.
Standing letters can tip. Check balance in the intended orientation. Use Desktop display to add a base or trim a flat bottom.

Checks reserve 0.8 mm beside each side of the strip and 2 mm behind its components. Actual strip bends, cut lengths, wiring, heat and lighting still need a physical check. Small or narrow font strokes may need separate LED pieces.

The edge gap is measured from the complete mount footprint (including the socket) to the outside edge or an internal opening. Auto-place favours the middle of each stroke. Light spread is not simulated.
Print the opaque front and sides as one body. The back stays open. Screw the printed standoff-pins to the wall, engage the large socket openings, then lower the letter 6 mm. Lift to remove.
At least three mounts per connected piece. Spread them across the shape where possible. This prototype is not load-rated or locked against lifting.
